probe: P3 - refusal evidence: what the contract refuses, and to whom
supersedes: the original F2 mechanism, which assumed KeeperHub would broadcast a doomed call. It does not - see docs/evidence/probe-2-revert-broadcast.json.

whatWasAvailable.constraint: guardRepay() is onlyAgent. The only address allowed to call it is the Turnkey EOA, whose key lives in an enclave. KeeperHub, the only party that can sign for that address, refuses to broadcast a call it predicts will revert. So the party that can broadcast will not, and the party that would has no key.
whatWasAvailable.resolution: Split the claim in two and prove each with the strongest evidence actually obtainable, rather than forcing one artifact that does not exist.

claim1_theContractRefusesTheAgent.assertion: When the agent asks the vault to defend a position that does not need defending, the vault refuses.
claim1_theContractRefusesTheAgent.evidence: KeeperHub execution records - real executionIds, the contract's own custom errors, decoded, carrying live arguments

records.reading: health 16667 was above the borrower's own trigger of 13000
already acted in oracle round 2 - one defensive action per round
no coupon accrued, so there is nothing to sweep

claim1_theContractRefusesTheAgent.honestLimit: These are KeeperHub execution records, NOT mined transactions. There is no BaseScan hash for them, because no transaction was ever broadcast. Say so plainly.

claim2_theContractRefusesEveryoneElse.assertion: Nobody outside the agent can make the vault act - not even the party that owns the entire rest of the system.
claim2_theContractRefusesEveryoneElse.method: cast send with an explicit --gas-limit, which skips gas estimation and therefore forces the doomed call onto the chain
claim2_theContractRefusesEveryoneElse.callerRole: deployer of every contract, owner of MockLendingPool, holder of the admin keys - the most privileged address in the system
claim2_theContractRefusesEveryoneElse.selectorCheck: cast sig "NotAgent(address)" == 0x52f49c95 - matches the first 4 bytes of the revert data

stateAfter.note: unchanged - a reverted transaction moves nothing

claim2_theContractRefusesEveryoneElse.reading: This is the strongest form of the authority claim. The person who deployed the system, owns the pool, can mint the tokens and register repayers, still cannot make a borrower's vault move a single unit. The vault answers to exactly one address, and that address is immutable.

claim3_exhaustiveness.assertion: The two refusals above are samples of a proven set, not lucky screenshots.
claim3_exhaustiveness.evidence: Foundry suite, 47/47 passing, with a dedicated test behind every Refused_* path and an ABI-surface fuzz test asserting the agent surface is exactly two zero-argument functions.

howToPresentThis.do: Say that KeeperHub declines to broadcast calls it predicts will revert - that is a safety property worth pointing at, and finding it is part of the work. Show the execution records for the agent-side refusals and the BaseScan link for the owner-side refusal.
howToPresentThis.doNot: Do not imply the agent's refusals have BaseScan hashes. Do not describe the NotAgent transaction as the agent being refused - it was the deployer being refused, which is a different and equally important claim.
howToPresentThis.prdImpact: PRD F2 still needs rewriting to match this. That is P4, deliberately deferred.
